projects.summary: A generative MIDI sequencer for Ableton Live. It plays a 16-step melody and changes it while it plays.
projects.imageAlt: Birds interface with colourful birds arranged on parallel wires
projects.title: Birds
projects.description:
## Context and constraints

The melody changes while it plays, so pitch, timing and note state had to stay readable as it changes. [needs: any other constraints, e.g. panel size]

## What I built

- A display where each note is a bird on one of 12 wires, one wire per pitch class. Clicking a bird switches its step on or off.
  - Colour states for original, drifted and muted notes. The playing bird is drawn in flight.
  - A Difference Limit control that sets how far the melody can drift from the original before it returns
  - Pitch and gate mutation strategies, and the manual

## Outcome

Covered by Rekkerd in April 2026. Sold on Gumroad and Isotonik Studios.

## Media

Carousel demo, full walkthrough (YouTube).

[needs: video captions and description of the sound]

about.subtitle: Berlin
about.body:
I'm Alessandro Miracapillo. I live in Berlin, I'm Italian, and I work in English and Italian. I make software for sound and image: music instruments and plugins, installations and web interfaces. I design the interfaces and write the code myself.

I build web frontends with React, TypeScript and Next.js, and backends with Node.js or Python (FastAPI) when a project needs them. In 2025 I developed the North Sea chapter of the Berggruen Institute's Planetary Compendium from the designers' Figma files. The project received an Honorary Mention at Prix Ars Electronica 2026. I also build sites for clients with headless CMSs such as PayloadCMS and PagesCMS.

Since 2018 I have run Aylesim Devices, where I design and build Max for Live instruments and support the people who use them. I studied electronic music at the Conservatorio Niccolò Piccinni in Bari, and I have made installations and live visuals.

## Awards
- Prix Ars Electronica 2026, Honorary Mention, Digital Humanity, for the Planetary Compendium (team project)
- Premio Nazionale delle Arti XV (Italian Ministry of University and Research), first prize, Electronic Art, 2021, for Please Set a Password

## Press
- Create Digital Music, "Free sounds and samples in Ableton Live, powered by commons and community", August 2020 (Freesound4Live)
- Rekkerd, "Aylesim releases Knob Studio experimental mapping device for Live", August 2024
- Rekkerd, "Birds generative MIDI sequencer for Ableton Live by Aylesim", April 2026

## Education
Diploma Accademico di I livello (bachelor's level) in Electronic Music, Conservatorio Niccolò Piccinni, Bari [needs year]

## Languages
Italian (native), English (professional)

[CV (PDF)](/cv.pdf) [Portfolio (PDF)](/portfolio.pdf)

[needs: CV PDF file]

## Community

**Max Berlin Network** (2025 to now). Founder & Organiser. I organise in-person meetups for Max/MSP users in Berlin, with demos, troubleshooting and shared patching, and I built the website, maxberlin.network.

## Teaching
- Fondazione Cascina Cotica (2024): a four-month remote web development course in Svelte, SvelteKit, Git and GitHub Pages for adults aged 20 to 60 with mixed starting levels. I reviewed code until every participant had a live website.
- La Scuola Open Source, Bari (2018 to 2026): worker-member of the cooperative. I ran workshops, including Self Playing Music (generative music in Max/MSP and Pure Data), ESP32 sensor builds at MAST Festival and Arduino at XFARM, and I maintained the cooperative's Kubernetes cluster (Docker, Nextcloud, Jitsi).

[needs: meetup photo]
